title: Near Earth Autonomy demonstrates hazard avoidance and adaptive mission execution on Black Hawk
summary: The demonstration integrated autonomous flight, environmental perception, and mission management.
body_markdown:
[Near Earth Autonomy](https://www.nearearth.aero/) (Near Earth) said it successfully demonstrated autonomous flight and mission execution capabilities on its[RUC-60 Black Hawk helicopter](https://www.nearearth.aero/responsive-uncrewed-capability-ruc-60) during a flight exercise on November 19 at Tullahoma Regional Airport, Tennessee.


Building on a series of U.S. Army-funded exercises, the demonstration featured autonomous obstacle avoidance during flight and landing, terrain following at 300 feet above ground level (AGL), and midflight retasking under remote operator supervision.


The demonstration integrated autonomous flight, environmental perception, and mission management.


Operators planned, initiated, and monitored missions from ground control stations (GCS) while the RUC-60 operated beyond visual line of sight (BVLOS). Operators issued mission changes, which the aircraft executed autonomously.


The aircraft also demonstrated autonomous takeoff and landing, evaluation of unprepared landing zones for slopes and hazards, and BVLOS operations with Loiter/Hold commands issued at distances greater than 45 nautical miles.


The demonstration integrated a long-range lidar sensor with the RUC-60’s onboard autonomy, extending the distance at which the aircraft can detect obstacles and respond to hazards through flight-path adjustments. Together with autonomous navigation, mission changes, and landings in unprepared areas, these capabilities support development of the RUC-60 to transport critical supplies in contested environments while reducing risk to aircrews.


“Our goal is to deliver critical supplies without putting aircrews in harm’s way,” said Sanjiv Singh, CEO of Near Earth Autonomy, “with the Army and our partners, we’re bringing together the capabilities needed for a utility helicopter to autonomously complete demanding logistics missions. This demonstration advances the aircraft’s ability to sense its environment, adapt to changing conditions, and execute missions under remote operator supervision, progressing towards systems ready to supply Warfighters in the field.”


Earlier 2026 flights demonstrated autonomous cross-country missions, responsive remote retasking, and safe landings in unprepared areas. The latest demonstration builds on these milestones by integrating additional perception and mission management capabilities to support increasingly complex operations.


The RUC-60 (Responsive Uncrewed Capability) is an optionally piloted UH-60L Black Hawk designed for high-capacity contested logistics, with a target cargo capacity of up to 8,000 pounds per load.


Under a U.S. Army Program Executive Office, Aviation (PEO Aviation) initiative, Near Earth is collaborating with Honeywell, Moog, and XP Services to transform existing Black Hawks into autonomous logistics aircraft.


The RUC-60 incorporates Near Earth’s[Captain autonomous pilot system](https://www.nearearth.aero/captain-autonomous-pilot-system) , a deterministic, safety-critical architecture designed to autonomously execute missions, manage risk, and respond to contingencies without requiring onboard aircrews, continuous remote piloting, or uninterrupted communications.


By retrofitting existing aircraft, the program aims to accelerate the availability of autonomous logistics capabilities for the Army.


“We look forward to continuing the RUC-60 product development,” said Samuel Dinnar, CSO of Near Earth Autonomy, “with a series of flight events in 2027 that will demonstrate the expansion of autonomous capabilities that will provide the users with more mission flexibility and confident ease of use.”


*This press release was prepared and distributed by Near Earth Autonomy.*
